subsystems.name: Hash function core
subsystems.role: provides the one-way and collision-resistant primitives on which all security rests.
parts: cryptographic hash such as SHA-256 or SHAKE

subsystems.name: One-time signature (OTS) scheme
subsystems.role: signs a single message (or a few) using a private key that must never be reused.
parts: signature revealing preimages or hash-chain values

subsystems.name: Merkle tree layer
subsystems.role: compresses many OTS public keys into one short public key.

subsystems.name: Hypertree / few-time layer
subsystems.role: allows a single public key to sign many messages without state.

subsystems.name: Key generation and management
subsystems.role: derives all secret values from a single seed and produces the public key.

subsystems.name: Signature generation and verification
subsystems.role: produces and checks signatures using the OTS and tree structures.

subsystems.name: Integration and hardening
subsystems.role: makes the scheme usable in real protocols and resistant to side-channel attack.

buildSteps.title: Pick hash function and security level
buildSteps.detail: Choose a hash such as SHA-256 or SHAKE and set n to 16, 24 or 32 bytes for 128-, 192- or 256-bit security.

buildSteps.title: Implement the one-time signature
buildSteps.detail: Build a Winternitz or Lamport scheme: derive secret values, hash them into public values, and define how a message digest plus checksum selects which secrets to reveal.

buildSteps.title: Build a Merkle tree over OTS keys
buildSteps.detail: Generate many OTS key pairs, hash each public key into a leaf, and combine leaves pairwise up to a single root — the public key.

buildSteps.title: Add a hypertree for stateless operation
buildSteps.detail: Stack several Merkle trees: the root of one layer is signed by an OTS in the layer above, so one key can sign many messages without tracking state.

buildSteps.title: Derive keys from a seed
buildSteps.detail: Use a pseudorandom function with a secret seed and a tree address to generate every OTS secret on demand, so the private key is just a short seed.

buildSteps.title: Generate a signature
buildSteps.detail: Hash the message, choose a random leaf index, produce the OTS signature for that leaf, and append the authentication path up to the root; repeat for each hypertree layer.

buildSteps.title: Verify a signature
buildSteps.detail: Recompute the OTS public key from the signature, hash it up the tree using the authentication path, and compare the result with the public root; repeat for each layer.

buildSteps.title: Harden and test
buildSteps.detail: Write constant-time code, avoid secret-dependent branches, and validate against published test vectors before deployment.

buildSteps.title: Integrate into protocols
buildSteps.detail: Embed the scheme in firmware signing, code signing or transport protocols, accepting larger signatures in exchange for conservative security.

prerequisites.why: the entire security proof reduces to hash preimage and collision resistance.
NIST finalised SLH-DSA as FIPS 205 in 2024, giving an interoperable stateless hash-based standard.

prerequisites.tech: Efficient Merkle tree and hypertree libraries
prerequisites.why: tree hashing and authentication paths must be fast enough for signing and verification.

prerequisites.tech: Secure random number generation and seed storage
prerequisites.why: a leaked or poorly generated seed compromises every signature.
hash-based schemes still leak through timing and power if not carefully coded.

prerequisites.tech: Tolerance for large signatures and keys
prerequisites.why: hash-based signatures are much larger than classical ones, so storage and bandwidth must accommodate them.

pathway.milestone: stateless hash-based signatures standardised and used in firmware and long-lived trust chains
pathway.unlocks: quantum-resistant authentication where conservative assumptions matter most.

pathway.milestone: support in hardware security modules, trusted platform modules and mainstream cryptographic libraries
pathway.unlocks: easy deployment in existing systems without custom code.

pathway.milestone: hybrid certificates and protocols combining classical and hash-based signatures
pathway.unlocks: a safe transition path that remains secure if either scheme is broken.

pathway.milestone: hardware accelerators and optimised verification for constrained devices
pathway.unlocks: wider use in embedded and high-volume verification settings.

pathway.milestone: hash-based signatures as a conservative fallback alongside lattice-based schemes
pathway.unlocks: defence in depth for decades-long data and infrastructure.
